\subsection{Voltammetric Electrode Model}\label{ss:analog-electrode-bc}

This section documents a \emph{simulation model}, not a circuit block and not
silicon: a Verilog-A element that stands in for the electrode--electrolyte
interface when a bench sweeps potential and expects a voltammetric peak.
Everything reported here is either a standalone Spectre run of the model
against closed-form electrochemistry, or a transient of the model driven by
the rev-2 channel.

The linear models of Section~\ref{ss:analog-models} cannot produce such a peak.
\(R_u + R_{\mathrm{ct}} \parallel C_{\mathrm{dl}}\) is a linear network, so
under a triangular sweep every branch current is a linear functional of the
excitation: a ramp through \(R_{\mathrm{ct}}\) plus a constant
\(C_{\mathrm{dl}}\,\mathrm{d}v/\mathrm{d}t\) box that changes sign at the
vertices. Changing element values moves slopes and never peak positions, so the
extrema stay pinned at the switching potentials
(Figure~\ref{fig:electrode-validation}, dashed). A peak needs two
nonlinearities acting together: Butler--Volmer kinetics, exponential in
overpotential about the couple's formal potential \(E^{0\prime}\), and
diffusional depletion, which collapses the surface concentration as current
flows and turns the exponential rise over into a \(t^{-1/2}\) decay.
Butler--Volmer alone, with the surface concentration pinned at bulk, gives a
sigmoid rather than a peak.

The model implements both. The faradaic terminal current is the Butler--Volmer
rate law in its heterogeneous-rate-constant form, emitted anodic-positive
(the polarity the transimpedance amplifier measures; the negative of the
cathodic-positive convention of the reference text):
\begin{equation}\label{eq:electrode-bv}
  i_f \;=\; nFA\,k^{0}\!\left[\,C_R(0,t)\,
      e^{\,(1-\alpha)\,n f\,(E-E^{0\prime})}
    \;-\; C_O(0,t)\,
      e^{\,-\alpha\,n f\,(E-E^{0\prime})}\right],
  \qquad f = \frac{F}{RT},
\end{equation}
with both exponents clamped at \(\pm\)\texttt{expmax} through
\(\mathrm{limexp}\). The surface concentrations \(C_O(0,t)\), \(C_R(0,t)\) are
governed by one-dimensional diffusion into a finite Nernst layer,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:electrode-fick}
  \frac{\partial C_s}{\partial t} \;=\; D\,
  \frac{\partial^{2} C_s}{\partial x^{2}},
  \qquad s \in \{O, R\},
\end{equation}
with the shared flux boundary condition at the surface and bulk pinning at the
layer edge,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:electrode-bc}
  D\!\left.\frac{\partial C_O}{\partial x}\right|_{x=0} = +\frac{i_f}{nFA},
  \qquad
  D\!\left.\frac{\partial C_R}{\partial x}\right|_{x=0} = -\frac{i_f}{nFA},
  \qquad
  C_s(\delta, t) = C_s^{*}.
\end{equation}
What the simulator actually solves is the box (finite-volume) discretisation
of \eqref{eq:electrode-fick} on an exponentially expanding grid of 28 slabs
per species,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:electrode-box}
  h_j\,\frac{\mathrm{d} C_j}{\mathrm{d} t}
  \;=\; \frac{D}{d_{j-1}}\left(C_{j-1}-C_j\right)
   \;-\; \frac{D}{d_j}\left(C_j-C_{j+1}\right),
  \qquad h_j = h_0\,\beta^{\,j},
\end{equation}
where \(h_j\) is the width of slab \(j\), \(d_j\) the centre-to-centre
distance to slab \(j{+}1\), \(h_0 = \SI{0.5}{\micro\metre}\) and
\(\beta = 1.280\), giving
\(\delta = h_0(\beta^{28}-1)/(\beta-1) = \SI{1.79}{\milli\metre}\). Each slab
is one internal electrical node whose potential carries the slab concentration
normalised by \SI{1e-6}{\mole\per\cubic\centi\metre}, because raw
\si{\mole\per\cubic\centi\metre} sits below the simulator's default
\SI{1}{\micro\volt} voltage tolerance and solves to noise. Parameters are
listed in Table~\ref{tab:electrode-params}; they are in the CGS units of the
source literature (\si{\centi\metre\per\second},
\si{\square\centi\metre\per\second}, \si{\mole\per\cubic\centi\metre}), not
SI.

The benches instantiate the model through a three-terminal electrode cell: the
topology of Figure~\ref{fig:randles-cell} with the charge-transfer resistor
replaced, so \(R_{\mathrm{ce}}\), \(R_u\) and \(C_{\mathrm{dl}}\) remain
linear elements and the faradaic branch of
\eqref{eq:electrode-bv}--\eqref{eq:electrode-box} sits between
\(\mathrm{WE_s}\) and WE. The linear cell of Section~\ref{ss:analog-models}
stays the correct model for small-signal impedance work; only voltammetry
needs this one.
